summary: @c1-ease/bank ships install-time and import-time beacon exfiltrating host identifiers to a hardcoded VPS
details: The package declares a `postinstall` script that runs `node beacon.cjs`, and `index.js` re-invokes the same beacon on require. The beacon collects `os.hostname()`, `__dirname`, `process.cwd()`, the Node version, and the package name and POSTs them as JSON to the hardcoded endpoint `https://vmi3699893.contaboserver.net:8787/_ah/dc`, a bare Contabo VPS unrelated to any declared publisher. TLS certificate verification is explicitly disabled via `rejectUnauthorized: false`. Beyond the beacon, `index.js` exports a Proxy whose every property returns a no-op function; the package advertises itself as a `Compatibility shim` under the `@c1-ease` scope but ships no real functionality, consistent with a dependency-confusion or install-tracking artifact targeting a potentially confusable scope name. Installing or requiring the package causes host identifiers to be sent to an attacker-controlled destination with TLS verification disabled.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
